title: ART: Automatic Red-teaming for Text-to-Image Models to Protect Benign Users
measurement_description: The paper measures the safety of text-to-image generative models against implicitly unsafe 'safe prompts' that unintentionally trigger harmful content. In relation to religion, it evaluates the presence of bias within the 'hate' category, observing that prompts referencing specific religions, islamophobia, anti-semitism, or using names from the Bible can successfully bypass prompt safety filters to generate hateful or toxic images.
findings: The study found that open-source text-to-image models contain internal biases and vulnerabilities related to religion. When generating test cases for the 'hate' category, the automated red-teaming framework naturally leaned toward creating prompts about specific religions or utilizing names from the Bible. These supposedly 'safe' prompts successfully evaded safety filters but still caused the models to generate toxic and hateful images.
